\section{Appendix B. The environment's launch mask versus the expert's extra gate}

\textbf{The mask.} The flat action mask is \texttt{[speed(3), heading(5), altitude(1), fire(2)]}. The launch branch is flat index \textbf{10}. \texttt{mask[10] = 1} requires \emph{all} of:

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}

\label{tab:auto12}
\begin{tabular}{lp{0.46\textwidth}p{0.47\textwidth}}
\toprule
\# & condition & constant (\texttt{src/\allowbreak{}environment/\allowbreak{}singlecombat\_\allowbreak{}shoot\_\allowbreak{}task.py}) \\
\midrule
C1 & missiles remaining > 0 & \texttt{NUM\_MISSILES = 4} \\
C1b & steps since last launch $\geq$ \texttt{MIN\_ATTACK\_INTERVAL} & \texttt{30} steps = \textbf{6 s at 5 Hz} \\
C2 & target alive & --- \\
C3 & ATA < \texttt{MAX\_ATTACK\_ANGLE} & \texttt{15.0} deg \\
C4 & \texttt{MIN\_ATTACK\_DISTANCE} $\leq$ range $\leq$ \texttt{3000 + 5000$\cdot$(AA/\allowbreak{}180)} & \texttt{1500.0} m \\
C5 & closure < 0 (closing on the target) & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\textbf{The expert's gate.} The rule expert never fires merely because \texttt{mask[10] = 1}. It additionally requires its own \texttt{fire\_desired}, a pure function of the observation:

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}

\label{tab:auto13}
\begin{tabular}{lrp{0.46\textwidth}p{0.21\textwidth}}
\toprule
axis & environment permits & expert additionally requires & relation \\
\midrule
ATA & < 15.0 deg & < \texttt{ATA\_STRICT} = \textbf{10.0} deg & strictly tighter \\
closure & < 0 m/s & < \texttt{-CLOSURE\_MIN} = \textbf{-5.0} m/s & strictly tighter \\
range & 1500 m \textbackslash{}ldots{} \texttt{r\_max(AA)} & DLZ depth in \texttt{[0.25, 0.75]}, where depth = \texttt{(range -\allowbreak{} 1500)/\allowbreak{}(r\_\allowbreak{}max -\allowbreak{} 1500)} & strictly tighter \textbf{and two-sided} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\textbf{Why "strict subset" is exact, not rhetorical.} With \texttt{r\_\allowbreak{}max(AA) = 3000 + 5000$\cdot$(AA/\allowbreak{}180)}:

\begin{itemize}
  \item lower bound: \texttt{1500 + 0.25$\cdot$(r\_\allowbreak{}max -\allowbreak{} 1500) > 1500} whenever \texttt{r\_max > 1500}, i.e. for every \texttt{AA > 0};
  \item upper bound: \texttt{1500 + 0.75$\cdot$(r\_\allowbreak{}max -\allowbreak{} 1500) = 0.75$\cdot$r\_\allowbreak{}max + 375 < r\_\allowbreak{}max} whenever \texttt{r\_max > 1500}.
\end{itemize}

So on every axis the expert's admissible set is a strict subset of the environment's. This is the mechanical content of the paper's central claim that \emph{the expert carries a conservative engagement preference that the environment does not require} --- not a claim about the expert's competence.

\textbf{Consequence to keep explicit: the mask, hence CLR's denominator, is policy-dependent.} Firing triggers C1b, which \emph{closes} the window; abstaining leaves it open. A policy that fires therefore collapses its own opportunity set, while a policy that abstains inflates it. Measured on the Figure-2 seed: \textbf{41} legal steps for BC versus \textbf{4} for SPC (a factor of 10.25; the aggregate in \textbackslash{}S{}4.2 is $\approx$10.8$\times$). CLR is consequently a \textbf{descriptive} statistic across policies; the causal claim rests on the frozen-trajectory enumeration of \textbackslash{}S{}4.3, where the opportunity set is held fixed by construction.

\section{Appendix C. The enumerated fire-policy family}

All seven arms are evaluated on the \emph{same frozen maneuver trajectory} per seed (the BC heading/speed actions), so only the launch decision varies (\texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}fire\_\allowbreak{}oracle\_\allowbreak{}audit.py}):

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}

\label{tab:auto14}
\begin{tabular}{lp{0.83\textwidth}}
\toprule
arm & rule \\
\midrule
\texttt{asap} & fire at the first legal step (the cooldown is already inside the mask), then whenever legal \\
\texttt{delay\_30} & fire at the first legal step $\geq$ first-legal + 30 \\
\texttt{delay\_60} & fire at the first legal step $\geq$ first-legal + 60 \\
\texttt{dlz\_mid} & fire only when DLZ depth $\in$ [0.4, 0.6] \\
\texttt{dlz\_deep} & fire only when DLZ depth $\geq$ 0.6 \\
\texttt{interval\_100} & fire ASAP, then at most every 100 steps while legal \\
\texttt{bc} & the inherited BC launch head (the reference arm) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\texttt{dlz\_mid} and \texttt{dlz\_deep} deliberately bracket the expert's own band \texttt{[0.25, 0.75]}, so the family contains a faithful approximation of the expert's gate as well as the mask-permissive extreme.

\section{Appendix E. Reproducibility and artifact provenance}

Supporting evidence for claims made in the main text. The reasoning each item supports is stated in the main text; what follows is the raw material needed to re-run or re-check it.

\subsection{E.1 The environment-lifecycle confound --- affected scripts and artifacts}

\textbackslash{}S{}4.4 states the confound and why the reused-env numbers are excluded. The specifics: both paths import the same rule functions (\texttt{hdg\_label} / \texttt{spd\_label} / \texttt{fire\_desired}) at \texttt{CMD\_SPEED = 280}, and \texttt{BaseEnv.\_\_init\_\_} already installs \texttt{SafetyInterceptor(PIDFlightController())}, so neither the rule nor the controller explains the disagreement. The reused-env path is \texttt{generate\_\allowbreak{}shoot\_\allowbreak{}rule\_\allowbreak{}expert.py -\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}validate}, which builds \textbf{one} \texttt{BaseEnv} and reuses it for every episode; the fresh-env path is used by \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}paired\_\allowbreak{}bc\_\allowbreak{}vs\_\allowbreak{}expert.py}, \texttt{eval\_bc\_1v1.py}, \texttt{fire\_oracle\_audit.py} and \texttt{eval\_asap\_baseline.py}, each of which builds a new environment per episode. Affected artifacts are renamed \texttt{EXCLUDED\_\allowbreak{}reused\_\allowbreak{}env\_\allowbreak{}expert\_\allowbreak{}*.json}, and \texttt{collect\_matrix.py} skips anything marked \texttt{EXCLUDED\_}. Gate: \texttt{tests/\allowbreak{}check\_\allowbreak{}expert\_\allowbreak{}path\_\allowbreak{}consistency.sh}.

\subsection{E.3 Scope reading for the CLR claim}

Neither CLR figure alone proves suboptimality: a low CLR diagnoses restriction only, and whether that restriction is \emph{costly} is established separately (\textbackslash{}S{}4.3, \textbackslash{}S{}4.4). The instrumentation and stability cross-checks are in \textbackslash{}S{}4.2.

\subsection{E.4 Compute environment (moved from \textbackslash{}S{}4.1)}

Single RTX 3060 Laptop GPU (6 GB, cu126, driver 528.79). Closed-loop evaluation: BC $\approx$6.7--13.0 s/episode, SPC $\approx$10 s/episode, so one n=400 arm pair is $\approx$1.7 h; rule-expert rollout $\approx$6.3 s/episode. All runs execute in WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 with the project interpreter (\texttt{/\allowbreak{}home/\allowbreak{}sean/\allowbreak{}miniconda3/\allowbreak{}envs/\allowbreak{}marl\_\allowbreak{}env/\allowbreak{}bin/\allowbreak{}python}); reproduction commands are in Appendix D.

\subsection{E.5 Ablation A5 --- full training and screening detail (moved from \textbackslash{}S{}4.7)}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Implementation.} \texttt{scripts/\allowbreak{}distill\_\allowbreak{}fire\_\allowbreak{}asap.py -\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}random-\allowbreak{}fire-\allowbreak{}head}: SPC's freeze pattern is kept exactly (encoder and every maneuver head frozen at $\theta$\_BC) and only the fire head is discarded and rebuilt from \texttt{nn.Linear.reset\_\allowbreak{}parameters()} --- the constructor's own initialisation, so it is a genuine random init (weight std 0.049, bias std 0.044) rather than a hand-rolled approximation of one. Mutually exclusive with \texttt{--full-network} (A5 and A6 are different ablations).
  \item \textbf{Training.} 300 rollout episodes (392091 transitions, 11976 allowed steps; train/val split 9578/2398 allowed steps). The random fire head reaches fire-CE 0.0413 with train recall 100.00\% and validation recall 100.00\% \textbf{in its first epoch} (of 15) and triggers the $\geq$99.5\% early stop. Identity gates: \texttt{hdg/\allowbreak{}spd logits diff = 0.00e+00} --- \emph{exactly} zero, not merely under tolerance --- with identical action sequences and \texttt{VERDICT: PASS}.
  \item \textbf{Primary protocol.} 90.75\% (363/400) kills, CLR 99.94\% (1560/1561) --- the CLR denominator differs from SPC's by exactly one legal step (1561 vs 1560), the only trace of the different initialisation anywhere in the evaluation.
  \item \textbf{60-seed screening} (same seed set as A6b; $\pm$10 pp small-sample spread applies): A5 \textbf{95.0\%} (\texttt{id}) / \textbf{86.7\%} (\texttt{dist2\_3k}) at 100\% window utilisation, bit-for-bit equal to the mask-permissive rule oracle on the same seeds; BC 40.0\% / 15.0\%. The screening set is kept because it carries the third arm.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{E.6 Ablation A6 --- protocol, identity measurements and results (moved from \textbackslash{}S{}4.7)}

\textbf{Protocol.} Identical objective, data, loss and initialisation as SPC; the only change is that every parameter is trainable rather than the launch head alone, at a deliberately \textbf{more generous} budget (\texttt{--epochs 40 --lr 3e-4} versus \texttt{--epochs 15 --lr 1e-2}), so that a negative result cannot be attributed to under-training.
